blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever uma carta ao editor sobre um problema social, com estruturas da unidade.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

frames.title: Reading · A letter to the editor

blocks.subject: Letter: Food banks are not a solution
paras: I am writing in response to your article on food banks. **It is estimated that** one family in six now relies on one. **Having been praised** as a safety net, food banks are, in my view, a symptom, not a cure.

**To a large extent**, the problem is low wages and rising rents. **The reduction** of benefits has made matters worse. I am **inclined to believe** that the government should **take** these factors **into consideration** before praising charity.

items.q: The writer believes food banks solve the problem.
One family in six relies on a food bank, it is estimated.

blocks.body: Numa carta ao editor: **abertura formal + dado + opinião + pedido**.

items.s: It is ___ that one in six families relies on one. (estimate)
___ been praised as a safety net, food banks… (Having)
The ___ of benefits has made matters worse. (reduce)
I am inclined ___ believe the law must change. (to)

blocks.task: Write a 7-sentence letter to the editor about a social problem in your area.
blocks.model: Dear Editor, I am writing in response to your article on homelessness. It is estimated that two hundred people sleep outside in our city each winter. Having been ignored for years, the problem is getting worse. To a large extent, it is a housing problem. The reduction of social housing has made matters worse. I urge the council to take these facts into consideration. Yours faithfully, Ana Lima
